title: A morpheme, in that chapter, is the smallest piece that means something
summary: OpenStax says a morpheme is the smallest unit that carries meaning, and that the English word I can be one.
body: In the OpenStax psychology chapter on language, the smallest piece that still means something is called a morpheme. The illustration is the English word I, which the authors say can stand alone as a meaningful piece. An ending that marks more than one, or an ending that marks the past, can also be a meaningful piece even when it is not a whole word. The chapter's explicit example remains I. This is a teaching definition. It does not inventory the pieces of any one language.

sources.title: Psychology, section 7.2 Language
sources.author: OpenStax
sources.note: First-edition web view at /books/psychology/, which the preface licenses CC BY 4.0. Opened 2026-11-26. No review date was printed on the section, so the source date is the access date. Paraphrase, with credit to OpenStax Psychology. Supports the morpheme definition and the example that I can be both a phoneme and a morpheme.
